## Key terms

{{< glossary streak gamblers-fallacy hot-hand-fallacy perceived-probability independent-events critical-hit drought shuffle-bag prd input-randomness output-randomness >}}

## 25.1 Real randomness is streaky

- k equal results **at one given place**: p^k^.
- In a long sequence, **some** long streak is very likely.
- 100 fair flips: the longest run is about 7; a run of 5+ in about 97 %.

![A person's sequence and a real coin.](images/streaks.png){width=94%}

{{< sim file="sims/streak-lab.html" poster="sims/streak-lab.png" title="Streak Lab: does random look random?" height="660" >}}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
One streak does not prove an unfair coin: look at many tries.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Streaks"}
Write 50 "random" H and T by hand; find your longest run. Then run Streak
Lab at 50 % five times and compare.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Streaks"}
Use Streak Lab. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="0 %|100 %"}
3 misses at one place, hit chance 0.7
:   0.3³ = 2.7 %

the usual longest run in 100 fair flips
:   about 7

a run of 5+ in 100 fair flips
:   about 97 % of the sequences

a run of 4+ misses in 100 attacks at 70 %
:   about 43 % of the fights
:::
:::

## 25.2 The gambler's fallacy and the hot hand

- Independent events: P(A | the past) = P(A).
- **Gambler's fallacy:** "heads is due". **Hot hand:** "I hit, so I will
  hit again".
- P(TTTTH) = 1/32, but P(H | TTTT) = 1/2.

![The coin has no memory.](images/no-memory.png){width=94%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
"If the player missed, roll again" changes the real chance.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Due or not?"}
After 3 misses at 70 %, is a hit sure? Is P(3 misses) under 3 %? Is a crit
after a crit more likely?
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · Fallacies"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="0|1"}
P(heads) after four tails
:   1/2

P(TTTTH) for a fair coin
:   1/32

"heads is due after many tails"
:   the gambler's fallacy

"I hit twice, so I will hit again"
:   the hot-hand fallacy
:::
:::

## 25.3 How players feel probabilities

- High chances feel **sure**; bad streaks are remembered.
- P(at least one miss in n) = 1 − p^n^.
- Test how a chance **feels**, not only the formula.

![A high chance still misses.](images/felt-chance.png){width=94%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
If a fair rule feels unfair, the rule or the way you show it needs work.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Feel the chance"}
p = 0.95: P(at least one miss) in 5, 10 and 20 attacks?
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · At least one miss"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="0.9|99 %"}
p = 0.9, at least one miss in 10
:   about 65 %

p = 0.9, at least one miss in 5
:   about 41 %

p = 0.95, at least one miss in 10
:   about 40 %

p = 0.7, at least one miss in 5
:   about 83 %
:::
:::

## 25.4 Shuffle bags

- A fixed set of results, shuffled, drawn **without putting back**; refill
  when empty.
- Exact share per bag; longest drought with 1 crit in n: **2(n − 1)**.
- The draws are not independent: on purpose.

![A shuffle bag.](images/shuffle-bag.png){width=94%}

{{< sim file="sims/bag-lab.html" poster="sims/bag-lab.png" title="Bag Lab: pure random, shuffle bag or PRD?" height="660" >}}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Small bags are predictable; big bags allow longer droughts.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Bags"}
In **Bag Lab**, compare pure random and the shuffle bag over 1000 players.
Then compute the longest drought for 2 crits in a bag of 8.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 4 · Bags"}
Use Bag Lab. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="25|no limit"}
crits in 100 attacks, bag of 4 with 1 crit
:   exactly 25

the longest drought, bag of 4 with 1 crit
:   6

the longest drought, bag of 5 with 1 crit
:   8

the longest drought, bag of 8 with 2 crits
:   12
:::
:::

## 25.5 Pseudo-random distribution (PRD)

- **P(N) = min(1, C · N)**, N = attacks since the last crit.
- C is chosen for the wanted average: C ≈ 0.085 for 25 %.
- A sure crit when C · N ≥ 1.

![PRD with C = 0.085.](images/prd.png){width=94%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
C = 0.25 does not give 25 %: compute or simulate C.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · PRD"}
Run PRD in **Bag Lab** for 1000 players; compute P(N) for N = 1, 4, 8 with
C = 0.085.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 5 · PRD"}
Choose the right answer (C = 0.085 unless given).

::: {.match extra="25 %|0 %"}
P(1)
:   8.5 %

P(8)
:   68 %

the attack with a sure crit
:   the 12th

C = 0.2: the attack with a sure crit
:   the 5th
:::
:::

## 25.6 Input or output randomness, and honest odds

- **Input randomness:** before the decision (map, cards); the player plans.
- **Output randomness:** after the decision (hit roll); exciting, can feel
  unfair.
- **Honest odds:** the shown chance is the real chance.

![Input and output randomness.](images/input-output.png){width=94%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Only output randomness makes skill feel unimportant.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Input or output?"}
Sort: a random map, a damage roll, the cards dealt, a random reward after a
level, the weather shown before a race.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 6 · Kinds of randomness"}
Choose the kind.

::: {.match extra="a seed|a matrix"}
a random dungeon map at the start
:   input randomness

the hit roll after an attack
:   output randomness

the cards dealt before the turn
:   input randomness

a random reward after a level
:   output randomness
:::
:::

## Game challenge: Fair or Frustrating? {.challenge}

Work alone. Use every section of today.

Six messages: **3 misses** at 70 %, **heads is due**, a **90 % miss**, crits
that **do not come**, the **sure crit** with PRD, and **odds** that do not
match the code.

{{< sim file="sims/fair-or-frustrating.html" poster="sims/fair-or-frustrating.png" title="Fair or Frustrating? Messages about luck" kind="game" height="440" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 7 · The messages"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="100 %|it is a bug"}
P(3 misses in a row) at 70 %
:   2.7 %

P(heads) after 4 tails
:   50 %

crits at 25 % with no long droughts
:   a shuffle bag or PRD

shown 5 %, code 1 %
:   dishonest: show the true odds
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 8 · Compute (harder)"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="0.5|1/16"}
0.2³ (3 misses at hit chance 0.8)
:   0.008

1 − 0.9⁵
:   about 0.41

PRD, C = 0.085, N = 6
:   0.51

the crit rate of a bag with 1 crit in 5
:   20 %
:::
:::

## Summary {.summary}

- Real randomness is streaky; one streak proves nothing.
- Independent tries have no memory: no "due" results.
- Players feel high chances as sure; compute 1 − p^n^ for many tries.
- Shuffle bags and PRD keep the rate and limit droughts.
- Prefer input randomness for skill; always show honest odds.
